clue.text: People bothered about language in Mass — those devoted to the Virgin

parts.note: a gram is a unit of mass
Marians are people with a special devotion to the Virgin Mary

explanation.surface: Fussy linguists are found at Mass among worshippers of the Virgin Mary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' with its capital looks like the church service, but it is the physical quantity measured in grams.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar specialists are scholars who worry over correct usage of words and sentences.

clue.text: Walk after a hearty breakfast?

parts.note: a condemned prisoner traditionally gets a hearty final breakfast before the short walk to be hanged

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a healthy post-breakfast stroll; the darker reading is the condemned man's last meal before execution.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to be led to execution, the final walk of a prisoner sentenced to hang.

clue.text: Girl seen in college put into a story

indicators.note: the college letter is placed within the phrase 'a story'

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story

explanation.surface: A girl at university gets written into a piece of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put into' puts C inside A LIE, splitting it after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, so a fair example of a girl.

clue.text: Dance company following society's conventions

indicators.note: the company abbreviation comes after the conventions in the answer

parts.note: mores are the customs and conventions of a society

explanation.surface: A dance troupe keeps to the social niceties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'society's conventions' looks like a phrase about manners; it is the Latin-derived word for customs, a word British solvers meet more in crosswords than in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The moresco is an old Moorish dance, related to the morris.

clue.text: Actor's car in colour Henry wouldn't allow!

definitions.note: read as 'Actor is', so the definition is simply an actor

parts.note: Henry Ford offered his cars in any colour so long as it was black, so red would not do
a Ford is a make of car

explanation.surface: An actor drives a car in a shade its maker would have banned.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's 'car in colour' is a red Ford; Henry Ford famously sold the Model T only in black.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Redford is a celebrated American film actor.

clue.text: Saw why Keith couldn't pick up Kate?

definitions.meaning: a saw is an old saying or proverb

definitions.text: why Keith couldn't pick up Kate?
definitions.meaning: Keith Richards is a member of the Rolling ... and Kate ... a model, so a rolling ... cannot gather ...

explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is not the tool but an old proverb; the second half jokes on the band and the model.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known proverb meaning a person always on the move never settles or accumulates anything.

clue.text: What could make one moan so — staginess in old play

indicators.note: the clue asks what a rearrangement of these words could produce

explanation.surface: A melodramatic groan is the sort of hamming you'd find in a classical drama.
explanation.walkthrough: MOAN SO and STAGINESS together are rearranged into the title, as 'What could make one' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's verse drama about Samson's last days is a play from the seventeenth century.

clue.text: Car registration set up for 5 23

parts.note: a Jag is a Jaguar car

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is read upwards

parts.note: REG is short for registration

explanation.surface: A personalised number plate is fitted to a car for a rock star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns REG into GER under JAG. '5 23' cross-refers to the linked answer, a member of the famous rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: Mick Jagger is the lead singer of the band the cross-reference names.

clue.text: Goddess sinking into bath energetically

indicators.note: the answer lies submerged within the words 'bath energetically'

explanation.surface: A goddess plunges vigorously into her bath.
explanation.definitionFit: Athene is the Greek goddess of wisdom, also called Athena.

clue.text: Worker is about to meet Her Maj, becoming more nervy

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's standard worker

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so 'is' is read backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen, Her Majesty

explanation.surface: A labourer gets jittery at the prospect of meeting the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes SI from 'is'; ER is the royal cipher of the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To have ants in your pants is to be jittery, so antsier means more on edge.

clue.text: Party men wanting dull, submissive type

parts.note: a do is a party
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men
mat (also matt) means dull, not glossy

explanation.surface: Lads at a bash who lack colour are pushovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'men' as OR (other ranks, soldiers below officer level) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A doormat is a person who lets others walk all over them.

clue.text: See 5
Wobbly toilet seat half falling off

parts.note: loo is British slang for toilet

indicators.note: the second half of the word seat drops away, leaving its first half

explanation.surface: A loose toilet seat is coming off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wobbly is not firmly fixed, the sense of slack or unsteady.

clue.text: Maverick has lost his heart in a dance

indicators.note: the central letter of the maverick's synonym is taken away

parts.note: a maverick is a rebel, an independent nonconformist

explanation.surface: A rebel loses his passion during a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has lost his heart' removes the middle B of REBEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a lively Scottish or Irish folk dance.

clue.text: One decants mucky liquid

indicators.note: mucky suggests the letters are messed about

explanation.surface: Someone pours a dirty fluid from one vessel to another.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ONE DECANTS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A condensate is the liquid formed when a vapour condenses.

clue.text: 19's uni?

parts.note: the racing driver whose surname is the 19 answer had a first name matching a Scottish university town

explanation.walkthrough: 19 is the surname of a famous British racing driver; his first name is also that of a Scottish university, so the clue puns on 'uni'.
explanation.definitionFit: The University of Stirling is in Scotland, and Stirling was racing driver Moss's first name.

clue.text: Try to engage with lunatic without saying much

indicators.note: the two words mesh together like gears, their letters interlocking into a new order

explanation.surface: Attempting to talk with a madman while barely speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of TRY and LUNATIC intermesh, which 'to engage with' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Taciturnly means in a reserved, uncommunicative manner.

clue.text: Bound to carry identification that's in good order

indicators.note: the bound synonym holds the identification within it

parts.note: tied means bound

explanation.surface: Someone obliged to carry papers keeps things orderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'obliged'; it is TIED, holding ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidied means put straight, arranged neatly.

clue.text: Cheese in bed girl's eaten

indicators.note: the girl's name swallows the bed word inside it

parts.note: Rita is a girl's name; the 's reads as 'has'
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A girl has eaten cheese in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'girl's eaten' reads as 'girl has eaten', so RITA takes in COT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft Italian whey cheese.

clue.text: Writer turning up to probe fat cat

indicators.note: the writer's name pokes into the fat word

parts.note: lard is pig fat

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means read from the bottom

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer

explanation.surface: An author investigates an overweight feline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' could be any pen or author; the short name of the American horror writer is the one that fits, and the reversal is upwards because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The leopard is a big spotted cat.

clue.text: See 5
Wife tucks into horse, fricasséed

indicators.note: the wife letter is tucked inside the horse word

parts.note: a steed is a horse

explanation.surface: A wife eats horse meat, cooked in a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucks into' hints at eating, but here puts W inside STEED.
explanation.definitionFit: A fricassee is meat stewed in sauce, so fricasséed means stewed.

clue.text: Yield of grass around about farm cut by 75%

indicators.note: about means surrounding the shortened farm
around tells us to turn the grass word backwards

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wetlands

indicators.note: three of the four letters of farm are cut, leaving the first

explanation.surface: The yield from a grassy field near a farm drops by three quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns REED into DEER; 'about' wraps that round F, from 'farm' 'cut by 75%'.
explanation.definitionFit: To defer is to give way or yield to another.

clue.text: Angry female's wrath in lively exchange

parts.note: cross means angry
F is the abbreviation for female
ire is wrath

explanation.surface: An angry woman's fury erupts in a heated argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossfire is a rapid exchange of remarks, by extension from gunfire.

clue.text: See 5
Conceited type is to get teased

indicators.note: teased as in hair or wool, pulled about into a new shape

explanation.surface: A vain person is bound to be mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: IS TO GET is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An egotist is someone excessively self-centred and vain.

clue.text: Issue not raised naturally

parts.note: issue means offspring, and this child was brought up by people other than the birth parents

explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a topic and 'raised' like bringing it up, but it is a child reared by others.
explanation.definitionFit: An adoptee is a child taken in and brought up by non-biological parents.

clue.text: Setters we can deal with?

parts.note: setters are dogs, so those who can manage them are trainers of dogs, not of crossword compilers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Setters' looks like crossword compilers; it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog handlers are people trained to control and work with dogs.
